reviewNotes: The ordinary timeout limit remains 240 seconds. Only Royale step 11 opts into a Windows-specific startup observation <=600 seconds with its original gameplay.phase == racing predicate. The normal A press is released after 16ms; fresh unchanged simulation must progress within 60 seconds, under the overall deadline. No clock/countdown/quality/game asset is modified.

Turbo step 4 retains original speed >2 plus course progress changed expectations. First matching fresh held state requires the same ID/session/cancel sequence, exact +1 raw press counter, actual semantic UP and advanced frame/input polls. It immediately sends the normal SDK release and requires two subsequent fully released fresh polls plus same-connection ACK accounting. Coasting after release does not erase the recorded original held-state proof.

Missing/stalled snapshots, unmet expectations, identity/cancel/focus/epoch changes, unexpected buttons and invalid ACK evidence fail; finally clears held SDK input. Bounded worker only reads native diagnostics and never writes game/model/store/clock. The unchanged SDK uses an RLock and a 2-second socket timeout; nested send sequence capture is reentrant. Network failure disconnects the SDK and cannot qualify as a pass.

The Windows gameplay override, after removing its single explicit opt-in branch and canonicalizing the existing plan module alias, is AST-identical to CatalogCheck.gameplay. No other ordinary/menuTap step changes. The initial reviewer AST lookup incorrectly selected the unrelated legacy Check.gameplay; correcting the class selector resolved that comparison without changing production source.
Backroad changes only step 32 timeout from 60 to 240; original keys, holdMs and phase predicate remain exact.
The existing CI lifecycle entrypoint imports both new test classes. Original combined 35-test and Android 6-test pass logs were inspected; the review did not rerun tests or native games.
limitations: Static review and source/evidence binding do not establish a new native Windows pass.
Original run 44615299245 failed reports remain failed and byte-identical.
